text_simplified: Children are a great amanah (trust) upon the necks of parents, and it is obligatory to give them tarbiyah (upbringing), guide them, and teach them good akhlaq (manners). This responsibility demands constant care and attention. Allah the Exalted says in the Qur'an regarding the qualities of the believers who preserve their amanahs.

review_defects.why: Arabic 'الآباء' specifically means fathers, not parents. The English 'parents' broadens the meaning to include mothers, altering who bears the responsibility described in the source.

review_defects.english: Tarbiyah of Children: A Great Amanah
review_defects.why: The Arabic title is a complete nominal sentence ('Raising children is a great trust'), while the English converts it into a noun phrase with a colon, losing the predicative structure and making it sound like a label rather than a statement.
